changes.before: Complete cachePolicy(scope). Exactly "public-catalog" returns "public, max-age=60". Every other scope returns "no-store". This exercise’s public catalog is explicitly nonpersonalized and contains no sensitive data.
changes.after: Allow shared caching only for the explicitly public catalog.

before: Caching reuses a previous response instead of always retrieving it again.
Cache-Control is a response header that tells caches how a response may be stored and reused.
public permits shared caching. max-age=60 sets a freshness lifetime of sixty seconds for this exercise.
A personalized or sensitive response must not be treated as the same public resource for everyone.
no-store asks caches not to store the response. It is not the same as no-cache, which permits storage but requires validation before reuse.
The practice uses an explicit public-catalog scope. Unknown scopes fall back to no-store rather than accidentally becoming cacheable.
The helper only chooses a string. A real HTTP test must inspect the actual response headers and ensure the public content is truly nonpersonalized.
A no-store response is not a complete privacy solution by itself. Authentication, access checks, transport and application storage remain separate responsibilities.
after: Caching stores a response so it can be reused later. It can reduce repeated work, but reusing the wrong person's response can expose private information.
Cache-Control is an HTTP response header: a named setting sent with the response. It tells caches how the response may be stored and reused.
This exercise's public-catalog content is the same for everyone and contains no sensitive data. public permits shared caching, and max-age=60 gives it a freshness lifetime of sixty seconds.
Personal or sensitive content must not be treated as this shared public catalog. A signed-out request alone does not prove the content is safe to share.
no-store tells caches not to store the response. no-cache has a different meaning: storage is allowed, but the cache must check with the server before reusing the response.
Recognize only the exact public-catalog name. Unknown scope names must fall back to no-store rather than accidentally allowing shared caching.
The function chooses a string. A real server must put that string in its Cache-Control header before sending the response. Check the actual header and confirm the content is truly public.
no-store is one storage instruction, not a complete privacy system. A real app still needs identity checks, permission checks, and protected connections.

before.question: A developer wants caches not to store a sensitive response. Why is no-cache not equivalent to no-store?
choices: no-cache may still permit storage, with validation before reuse.
no-cache always deletes every copy on every device.
before.explanation: The directives have different meanings. Preventing storage is not the same as requiring revalidation before reusing stored content.

after.question: Why is no-cache different from no-store?
choices: no-cache can allow storage but requires checking before reuse
no-cache deletes every copy on every device
Both remove the need for authentication
after.explanation: Preventing storage and checking before reuse are different rules.
